findings: Large-phone first eight panels: pictures and controls are clear and fit captured viewports; movement supporting text remains smaller than the child instruction.
Tablet portrait first four panels: legible pictures and instructions; six counting tiles wrap five plus one.
Tablet landscape first four panels: narrative opening image pushes rhyme text and return control below the captured viewport; needs separate full-scroll review. Other three panels fit.
Desktop first four panels: story text beside picture and return controls fit; two-word preview is labeled possibly stale.

Scroll sheet 001: three states and their paired top/bottom captures inspected, with readable text, image and reachable return control; no overlap seen. Dot-grid versus finger instruction remains an existing pedagogical finding.

Scroll sheets 002–006: fifteen states and their paired captures inspected. Counting controls and return controls remain reachable; no clipping or overlap was found. The m1-math-01 reset capture is historical evidence from before VIS-FIX-01.

Large-phone sheet 002: all eight panels fit. The physical-activity support steps remain comparatively small, and the Lisa opening image reveals the bucket location before the later question; both are existing review findings. The story-counter capture is labeled stale.
Tablet portrait, tablet landscape and desktop sheet 002: all twelve panels fit without clipping. Movement support text is relatively small at distance; the two-word preview is labeled possibly stale.

Scroll sheets 007–016: Claude Max/Opus inspected all thirty states; Astra independently inspected the claimed defect and representative counting, reset, rhyme and navigation states. No new product defect was accepted. Counts, highlights and answer feedback remain consistent, and every control is reachable in a paired frame.

Scroll sheet 015: grey borders that move between paired frames are CSS hover borders, caused by the capture script scrolling content beneath a stationary pointer. Stable orange and green answer borders confirm that this is capture noise rather than misleading application state.

The repeated number activities and repeated « Je marche, je m’arrête » rhyme are established, previously reviewed curriculum content, not evidence of a visual regression. Existing finger-versus-dot and rhyme-image pedagogy findings remain unchanged and unapproved.

Initial sheet 003 across all four viewports: all twenty panels are readable and controls remain reachable. Tablet-landscape narrative content continues below its initial viewport as expected and is covered by full-scroll evidence. Movement support text remains relatively small; no new clipping or overlap was found.

Scroll sheets 017–021: all fifteen states inspected locally. Count values and highlighted objects agree, success controls remain reachable in the lower paired frame, and Tika story navigation plus rhyme return controls are reachable. No new clipping or overlap was found.

Scroll sheet 018 repeats the already recorded bucket-on-chair mismatch for « Le petit seau »; scroll sheet 019 has a coherent rain illustration and a readable one-line story counter. These do not add a new finding.

Initial sheet 004 across all four viewports: all twenty panels inspected. Phone, portrait and desktop layouts fit. The tablet-landscape story and rhyme continue below the initial viewport, consistent with prior narrative behavior; the initial capture alone is not treated as full-scroll evidence. The Lisa bucket image remains an existing pedagogical finding.

Scroll sheets 022–031: Claude Max/Opus inspected all thirty states; Astra independently inspected the reported triangle issue, representative sort placement, final counting and story navigation. No new clipping, overlap or reachability defect was found.

m1-math-16-a1 contains a triangle but only « les ronds » and « les carrés » groups. This is a genuine interaction/pedagogical correctness issue, but it is already recorded as open in astra-manual-interaction-review.json. Approved content is unchanged pending a bounded pedagogical decision.

Placed group-and-match tokens are approximately 20 px wide on a 320 px phone and low prominence inside large drop zones. This is accepted as a HIGH_VALUE_IMPROVEMENT candidate for the later systemic design pass, not a blocker for evidence review.

Initial sheet 005 across all four viewports: all twenty panels inspected and all controls fit. The phone m1-phys-06-a1 screen says « Lance la balle dans le seau » but displays generic « courir / s’arrêter / recommencer » steps. This is a content/display semantic defect and must not be silently corrected without reconfirmation.

Scroll sheets 032–041: Claude Max/Opus inspected all thirty states; Astra independently inspected the missing-article defect and representative count/sort states. Count and sort continuity, feedback and control reachability pass. m1-math-19 repeats the already-open triangle-group defect.

m1-world-20-a1 renders bare media tags as French target labels, producing « Montre : main » and « C’est celui-ci : main. » This is a confirmed renderer/data-label DEFECT; the generic label strategy needs a systemic solution rather than a lesson-text patch.

Claude's note that the counted object in m1-math-20-a1 was ambiguous was rejected after inspecting the source-resolution sheet: the spoon is recognizable. The weak action depiction in « Je marche, je m’arrête » remains part of the existing illustration-semantic finding.

Initial sheet 006 across all four viewports: all twenty panels inspected and controls fit. m1-phys-08-a1 repeats the approved ball-throw/generic-running-steps defect. Body-part pictures are clear; the hands-on spoon remains small but recognizable.

Initial sheets 007–008 across all four viewports: all forty panels inspected. Controls and content fit on phone, portrait and desktop. Tablet-landscape narrative content can continue below the initial viewport and remains covered by scroll evidence. m1-phys-09-a1 and m1-phys-10-a1 prove the generic movement-step mismatch is broader than ball activities; the repeated 1ère payload needs a bounded content audit.

Scroll sheets 042–061: Claude Max/Opus inspected all sixty states; Astra independently inspected all three claimed defects and their source paths. Count, story, choice and sort continuity remain intact, and controls are reachable in overlapping frames.

m3-lang-02-a2 renders sentence stems as empty picture cards because seven vocabulary entries are paired positionally with only five media assets. Its generic choice game also uses the hardcoded shape retry « Regarde bien la forme ». Both are renderer-level DEFECTS suitable for the systemic design pass.

m3-math-02-a2 asks for the same number as the adult's pile of four, but the child renderer presents six tappable dots and celebrates six without showing or comparing the model pile. This is a pedagogical-integrity DEFECT; approved data and success semantics remain unchanged pending a bounded decision.

Claude's notes about missing story illustrations, isolated French punctuation wraps and moving hover borders were kept as optional polish or capture artifacts. They do not justify implementation during evidence review.

Initial sheets 009–012 across all four viewports: all eighty panels inspected. Phone, portrait and desktop content fits; tablet-landscape narrative cards can continue below the initial viewport as already covered by scroll evidence. The repeated generic 1ère movement steps, bare ChooseOne labels, triangle-without-group case, dot-grid/finger conflict and story-image issues are already classified; no new initial-screen defect was added.

Scroll sheets 062–081: Claude Max/Opus inspected all sixty states; Astra independently inspected each claimed defect and the corresponding approved payload. Story, count and choice state continuity passes and controls remain reachable in overlapping frames.

The generic counting renderer erases task-defining structure in four approved activities: matching an adult's pile, lining objects up, counting separate mine/yours sets and counting objects arranged in a circle. This is one systemic pedagogical-integrity DEFECT, not four isolated visual preferences.

m3-math-03-a2 uses fixed shape labels while accepting mismatched placements and praising completion. This is a genuine feedback-semantics DEFECT. The intended open-versus-checked sorting model needs a bounded pedagogical decision before implementation.

Initial sheets 013–014 across all four viewports: all forty panels inspected. The layouts fit except for expected tablet-landscape narrative continuation covered by scroll evidence. Only already-classified movement, dot-grid/finger and triangle-group findings recur.

Scroll sheets 082–101: Claude Max/Opus inspected all sixty states; Astra independently inspected every new defect against the approved payload. Stories, ordinary count continuity, resets and navigation remain coherent and reachable.
m3-math-08-a1 loses its comparison model and becomes a written-name choice task; m3-math-08-a2 replaces open room observation with a graded fixed square. Both are genuine renderer/semantics DEFECTS.

m3-math-10-a1 changes counting from 10–20 into 1–20 and separates its running count from early taps by two phone screens. The sequence error is a DEFECT; persistent/compact feedback is a HIGH_VALUE_IMPROVEMENT.

The singular reveal copy when two rotated variants are accepted and isolated French punctuation wraps are OPTIONAL_POLISH. The Kumu reference is not a defect: Kumu was introduced earlier in the month.

classifiedFindings.evidence: Placed shapes are approximately 20 px wide inside large group zones at 320 px, making the result hard for a preschool child to recognize.
classifiedFindings.scope: GroupAndMatch child renderer; no approved content change.

classifiedFindings.evidence: The triangle can only be placed into « les ronds » or « les carrés » while the instruction asks for the same shape.
classifiedFindings.scope: Approved activity data; preserve digest and require bounded pedagogical decision before editing.

classifiedFindings.evidence: The 1ère movement payload repeats « courir / s’arrêter / recommencer » across days regardless of the approved instruction. Confirmed mismatches include throwing a ball into a bucket (m1-phys-06-a1 and m1-phys-08-a1) and walking to a marker then returning (m1-phys-09-a1 and m1-phys-10-a1).
classifiedFindings.scope: Approved 1ère movement payloads; audit all instances and require bounded pedagogical reconfirmation before editing.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m1-world-20-a1 renders « Montre : main » and « C’est celui-ci : main. » because generic ChooseOne labels fall back to bare media tags.
classifiedFindings.scope: Renderer/media-label architecture; preserve approved lesson text and solve French display labels systematically.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-lang-02-a2 includes « il sert à » and « elle sert à » after five pictured words; the word-card renderer gives both sentence stems empty image slots, making them look broken.
classifiedFindings.scope: Word-card vocabulary/media pairing; preserve approved vocabulary and render non-picture sentence frames intentionally.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-lang-02-a2 is an object vocabulary choice game, but its retry says « Regarde bien la forme » because ChooseOne hardcodes shape-specific feedback.
classifiedFindings.scope: Generic ChooseOne feedback architecture; use context-appropriate wording without changing approved lesson instructions.

classifiedFindings.evidence: The generic counting screen turns distinct approved tasks into the same tappable grid: m3-math-02-a2 loses the adult's model; m3-math-05-a1 loses the line; m3-math-06-a2 collapses mine/yours; m3-math-07-a2 loses the circle; and m3-math-11-a2 cannot split five objects into two piles or try another split.
classifiedFindings.scope: Counting renderer and approved activity semantics; requires a bounded pedagogical decision before changing layout, data or success behavior.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-03-a2 labels four bins by shape, accepts visibly mismatched placements, states there is no wrong answer, then says « Tout est rangé. Bravo ! » when every token has merely been placed.
classifiedFindings.scope: GroupAndMatch feedback contract and approved sorting pedagogy; decide between open unlabelled sorting and checked labelled groups before implementation.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-08-a1 asks the child to find the shape matching « celle-ci », and its approved guidance requires comparing differently sized/oriented pairs, but the child screen shows no model shape and instead asks « Montre : carré ».
classifiedFindings.scope: Matching renderer and approved comparison semantics; provide an explicit model/pair interaction without altering the approved instruction.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-08-a2 asks the child to find and name a shape in the room, but the child screen requires selecting a predetermined on-screen square and grades that tap.
classifiedFindings.scope: Observation renderer and mode semantics; preserve the approved real-world task and avoid inventing a fixed answer.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-10-a1 is « De dix à vingt », but the child counter starts at 1, passes through 10 without a transition and finishes at 20, changing the practiced sequence to 1–20.
classifiedFindings.scope: Counting renderer and approved sequence semantics; require a bounded pedagogical design for the given first ten and the 10–20 transition.

classifiedFindings.evidence: At 320×740, the twenty-item count grid is about three screens tall; the running count and reset control are two screens below the first targets, so action and feedback cannot be seen together.
classifiedFindings.scope: Long CountTogether layouts; keep live progress visible through a denser layout or persistent feedback.
